claims.text: The combined ML-interatomic-potential, Green–Kubo MD, and electronic Boltzmann-transport approach will predict total thermal conductivity within ±5% of experiment from 100 to 1200 K.
The proposed approach will reduce average prediction error by at least 15% relative to prior DFT-plus-analytical models.
A machine-learned interatomic potential can capture atomic-scale mass and force-constant disorder in HfNbTaTiZr.
Green–Kubo molecular dynamics will separately calculate the phononic contribution to thermal conductivity.
Boltzmann-transport calculations will separately calculate the electronic contribution to thermal conductivity.
Separately simulating phononic and electronic transport provides an explicit decomposition of total thermal conductivity.
The target material is bulk equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with less than 0.1 wt.% oxygen and minimal point defects.
Prior DFT-derived analytical conductivity models typically have ±20% error over 100–1200 K.
The proposed model is applicable to defect-free samples at temperatures up to 1200 K.
The proposed model is not expected to remain valid above 1200 K.
The proposed model is not expected to remain valid when oxygen content exceeds 1 wt.%.
Residual fitting errors in the ML potential produce an uncertainty of ±5%.
Prediction uncertainty may increase near 100 K and near 1200 K.
Four-probe electrical measurements combined with the Wiedemann–Franz law can infer the electronic contribution, allowing the lattice contribution to be separated from total conductivity.
The hypothesis is falsified if predicted total conductivity differs from experiment by more than ±10% at two or more temperatures between 100 and 1200 K.

contradictions.description: The prediction is claimed to be accurate within ±5%, but the stated falsification rule permits deviations between 5% and 10% without falsifying it. Thus, the decisive threshold does not directly test the claimed accuracy bound.
The primary sample scope requires less than 0.1 wt.% oxygen, whereas the boundary only excludes oxygen contents above 1 wt.%, leaving applicability from 0.1 to 1 wt.% oxygen ambiguous.
